placement: after several principal characters have established professional identities; provisional 2031-2033 window
premise: A fictional cross-institution health-data pilot uses a survival-risk scoring workflow to prioritize manual follow-up. A routine batch produces a suspicious low-risk list. During manual review, several records prove to have been scored under inconsistent data/version conditions. Before the institutions agree on what happened, a screenshot of the list leaks outside the project. A 72-hour explanation is demanded.

inciting_object.object: a one-page exported risk list with several rows circled by hand
inciting_object.visual_hook: one row is marked low-risk although the follow-up record is obviously incomplete; another row has two different score timestamps
inciting_object.reader_question: Is this a bad model, bad data, a deployment/version problem, or a process failure?
inciting_object.important_rule: The answer must not be available in the opening chapter. Different pieces are held by different institutions.

central_clock.first_deadline: 72 hours for a joint preliminary explanation
central_clock.second_deadline: one week to decide whether the pilot pauses, narrows, or continues
central_clock.long_tail: audit, responsibility allocation, scientific correction, career consequences and trust damage continue for months

central_question: When data, model, code, deployment and decision authority are split across institutions, who is responsible for a wrong-looking result before anyone even agrees on what went wrong?

factions.public_goal: protect patients and determine whether the pilot can safely continue
factions.private_pressure: a politically visible pilot cannot appear uncontrolled
factions.reasonable_position: do not create public panic before the failure mode is verified
factions.shadow: may compress uncertainty into an administratively convenient explanation

factions.public_goal: protect clinical interpretation and data integrity
factions.private_pressure: does not want incomplete follow-up or local data processes blamed publicly
factions.reasonable_position: model developers cannot ignore how data are actually produced
factions.shadow: may treat every anomaly as an upstream model problem

factions.public_goal: identify whether the statistical method is valid under the observed censoring and missingness pattern
factions.private_pressure: scientific credibility, publication claims and professional identity are exposed
factions.reasonable_position: deployment should not be judged as if it were the original research setting
factions.shadow: may define the failure narrowly enough to protect the method

factions.reasonable_position: a model cannot be audited without knowing exactly which data and code version ran
factions.shadow: may reduce a substantive statistical issue to a version-control issue

factions.public_goal: understand whether the anomaly affects ongoing analyses and timelines
factions.private_pressure: delays cost money and may affect downstream regulatory or business decisions
factions.reasonable_position: uncertainty must eventually be translated into a decision, not left as an academic caveat
factions.shadow: may push for a binary answer before the evidence supports one

factions.public_goal: reproduce the anomaly before blame is assigned
factions.private_pressure: limited authority, incomplete access, and the risk of being used as neutral decoration
factions.reasonable_position: no causal story should be accepted without a reproducible path
factions.shadow: verification can become delay if it never reaches a decision threshold

factions.public_goal: ask why a patient-facing or policy-facing system produced a suspicious list
factions.private_pressure: needs a comprehensible story under deadline
factions.reasonable_position: institutions often hide behind technical complexity
factions.shadow: may prematurely personalize a distributed failure into a villain story

luo_cheng.dramatic_use: he understands the chain of documents, meetings and responsibility handoffs but initially lacks authority; he becomes useful because he remembers who knew what when
luo_cheng.conflict: process loyalty versus the temptation to protect people he works with

gao_yuan.dramatic_use: must help turn technical uncertainty into an actionable briefing
gao_yuan.conflict: careful stability-seeking style is rewarded by procedure but may become institutional caution at the wrong moment

zhou_ye.dramatic_use: version logs and reproducibility become materially important, but his competence creates pressure for him to become the single person everyone calls
zhou_ye.conflict: being indispensable helps solve the crisis while deepening the very dependency his long arc later resists

tang_yu.dramatic_use: recognizes that a censoring/missingness condition may invalidate a comfortable interpretation
tang_yu.conflict: the scientifically honest answer may damage work close to her intellectual identity; negative evidence gains real external stakes

he_xin.dramatic_use: sees the practical difference between a procedural pause and an institutional cover-up
he_xin.conflict: her skill at making systems tolerable can either protect due process or help a bad equilibrium persist

song_nan.dramatic_use: must explain what the uncertainty changes for a real decision and deadline
song_nan.conflict: her speed and decisiveness are valuable, but she can compress nuance too aggressively when others are slow

xu_hang.dramatic_use: tries to reconstruct the exact failure path and demands stop rules for claims
xu_hang.conflict: verification finally becomes central rather than auxiliary, but everyone wants him to certify more than the evidence warrants

chen_lan.dramatic_use: can see where high-response organizational habits distort the investigation
chen_lan.conflict: her boundary discipline is tested when the crisis genuinely may require unusual response

opening_design.principle: begin with the abnormal object and a person forced to act, not with a world-history explanation
opening_design.possible_first_image: a printer produces the one-page risk list before the office fully opens; three rows are already circled in red by someone who arrived earlier
opening_design.possible_first_action: the first focal actor is told not to forward the list and then immediately receives a message from someone outside the room who already has a screenshot
opening_design.first_chapter_job: establish that the list exists, that different people already know different pieces, and that a 72-hour clock has started

causal_spine: internal attempt to classify the anomaly
version/data/method evidence begins to contradict convenient narratives
responsibility shifts from individual error to distributed system design
characters make choices that protect different goods
pilot decision is made before complete certainty exists
later audit reveals what was knowable at each stage and who acted anyway
anti-thriller-cheat_rules: No omniscient villain secretly caused everything.
No single technical bug explains the entire incident.
No faction is stupid merely to create conflict.
Every major position must protect something genuinely valuable.
The technical answer and the moral/responsibility answer are not required to be identical.
The final truth may be distributed: data delay plus version mismatch plus an invalid assumption plus deadline pressure can jointly create the event.
status_note: This is a provisional central engine for adaptation testing. It does not overwrite the frozen historical ledger and should not yet be treated as prose canon.
